title: Citation traceability — a chain from the note to the source
titleEs: Trazabilidad de una cita — Microescena con objetos y actores
description: First-person library bay: a brass chain hooks onto the footnote of an article, runs to the intermediate reference that the researcher’s hand pulls from its shelf and opens on a cradle, then from that book’s own footnote to the original entry the hand lifts out of an archive box. Supplied final state: traced to the source, or only to the intermediate (original unopened, dashed cited-in link). Descriptive only.

durationMs.description: Total length of the finite timeline in milliseconds. Phases scale proportionally; the final state is held.

seed.description: Seed for small deterministic variations (appearance defaults, hand-drawn jitter). Same seed + time + params = same frame.

locale.description: Language of built-in labels (en or es). User-supplied text is never translated.

theme.description: Render treatment. Only tested themes are listed.

palette.description: Colour palette applied to props, actors and accents.

background.description: transparent, paper, white, light-grey, charcoal or a #rrggbb colour.

safeArea.description: Caption-safe margins as fractions of the frame.

reducedMotion.description: Removes decorative motion (overshoot, idle sway, camera drift) while keeping instructional motion.

textVisibility.description: all labels, key labels only, or none (the action must remain readable without labels).

jurisdiction.description: Descriptive jurisdiction tag. "unspecified" means no legal system is asserted.

contentNotice.description: Shows a small "illustrative example" tag inside the safe area.

query.description: Text typed into the catalogue search (buscador); by default the work named in the note (fictional)

article.description: Citing work whose footnote starts the trail (printed in the article header and on the card)

intermediate.description: Intermediate reference: the work the note cites; it cites the source in turn (cover, page header, search result, card)

source.description: Source document: the original the intermediate reference cites (folio header, card)

sources.description: The three works on the citation trail (fictional titles, never real works)

noteNumber.description: Footnote number in the citing article

pinpoint.description: Place in the intermediate reference cited by the note, e.g. "p. 88" (printed in the note and as the page number of the open page)

innerNote.description: Footnote number inside the intermediate reference

folio.description: Place in the source document cited by the intermediate, e.g. "fol. 14" (printed in its footnote and on the folio)

entry.description: Entry of the source document the trail ends on: "1"–"4" selects the numbered entry on the folio (other text is printed on the third entry)

shelfMark.description: Shelf mark returned by the catalogue search and printed on the shelf plate

citations.description: How each stop cites the next. Composed into the footnotes as "<work>, <place>"; fictional references only, never real citations

article.description: Date printed in the article header

intermediate.description: Edition/date printed on the intermediate reference

source.description: Date written on the source entry

dates.description: Fictional, relative date labels printed on each work

researcher.description: Caption shown at the researcher’s hands

actorLabels.description: Caption for the first-person researcher (whose hands act)

search.description: Title of the catalogue search screen

card.description: Title printed on the citation-trail card (ficha)

box.description: Label on the archive box that holds the original

actionProgress.description: How far the concrete action is allowed to progress (1 = complete; lower values freeze it part-way)

target.description: Scene element the annotation points at

items.description: Editorial annotation shown during the hold

annotations.description: Editorial callouts shown in the final hold (array replaces the previous value)

finalState.description: State supplied for the final hold: source-reached (the chain reaches the opened original) or intermediate-only (the chain ends at the intermediate reference; the original stays unopened). No judgement on the citation is inferred

annotations.text: The chain ends on the entry the treatise cites
